## Cause
In `ModelAdmin.get_search_results()` (`django/contrib/admin/options.py`), each word of the search query was applied as its own `queryset = queryset.filter(or_queries)` call. Every chained `filter()` spanning a relation (`clientoffice__name`, …) makes the ORM add a **fresh JOIN to the same table** instead of reusing one — so an N-word search over `Client` with `clientoffice__*` in `search_fields` produced N joins on `clientoffice` (3-word search: 3 JOINs), which stalls on large tables (the #15022 scenario).

## Fix (minimal, source only — no tests touched, not committed)
`django/contrib/admin/options.py`, 3 insertions / 1 deletion: collect each term's OR-Q in a `term_queries` list and apply **one** `filter(models.Q(*term_queries))` (AND across terms) instead of one `filter()` per term. This is byte-identical to Django's own upstream fix for this issue (commit `76ccce64cc`, ticket #16063, released in Django 4.1 — `git diff 76ccce64cc -- django/contrib/admin/options.py` is empty).
